pr_title: Update toolchain resolution to load requested toolchain types.
pr_body:
This allows Bazel to validate toolchain types earleir, and to deal with
aliases to toolchain types.

Fixes #7404.
pr_comments: CC @brandjon and @hlopko, who were wondering about this.

Sure. Currently, it doesn't resolve the toolchain type labels directly: ToolchainResolutionFunction calls SingleToolchainResolutionFunction, which calls RegisteredToolchainsFunction. RTF returns the ToolchainTypeInfo providers, and the labels from those are directly compared to the labels that were requested.

This breaks when the label in the rule are aliases, because the alias labels don't match the labels in the ToolchainTypeInfo.

issue_context.title: Toolchain types should be aliasable
issue_context.body:
Suppose you define a `toolchain_type` with label `"//pkg:tt"`, and an `alias` that points to it named `"//tt2"`. Then you should be able to use either `//pkg:tt` and `//pkg:tt2`interchangeably. This is important for smooth migration of `toolchain_type` definitions from one name/package/repository to another.

Currently this works for a `toolchain` target's `toolchain_type` attribute: When you specify `//pkg:tt2`, it retrieves the original `ToolchainTypeInfo` provider from the `alias` target and sees the original `//pkg:tt` label.

It does not work for a rule that declares a required toolchain type of `//pkg:tt2`. The problem can be traced back to the fact that [ToolchainResolutionFunction](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/fcf46b2f781cecd4c2003633fe2de745c0fa1044/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/skyframe/ToolchainResolutionFunction.java#L132) directly compares the label of the requested toolchain type, when it should instead resolve this label to a configured target and retrieve the label in the `ToolchainTypeInfo` provider.
comments: Note that once this is fixed, it would still not be expected that you can require a toolchain type under one name but retrieve it from `ctx.toolchains` under another.
This seems related to the concerns @aragos has about constraint values proliferating.

How so? I did a cursory check, and aliasing appears to be fully transparent to constraint values and constraint settings.

Or are you referring to the problem of explicitly merging two distinct constraint values that are not declared as aliases?
I meant the latter, which won't directly involve alias rules, but which is conceptually related.
